headline: Underwriting gains lift adjusted profit, GAAP EPS cools q/q
summary_short: MetLife's Q2 FY2026 net income was $736M (diluted EPS $1.09), while adjusted earnings rose 15% y/y to $1.6 billion ($2.43/share, +20%) on 7% growth in premiums, fees and other revenues to $13.7 billion.
summary_long: Adjusted earnings rose 15% y/y (14% constant-currency) to $1.6B, or $2.43/share (+20%), driven by favorable underwriting and broad-based volume growth; GAAP net income was $736M ($1.10 basic EPS), down sharply q/q against an unusually strong Q1 but up modestly y/y. Premiums, fees and other revenues grew 7% y/y to $13.7B; net investment income rose 18% to $6.7B on higher asset valuations. All five business segments posted higher adjusted earnings, led by Group Benefits (+25%) and Asia (+21%, +25% constant-currency). Book value per share rose 8% y/y to $38.59. MetLife returned $1.1B to shareholders via $700M of buybacks and roughly $400M of dividends this quarter; holding-company cash of $3.4B remained within its target range. No numeric forward guidance was issued.

The release's $705M/$1.09 EPS pairing is internally consistent (both from the same GAAP table), while the resolver's basic EPS tag (SEC XBRL EarningsPerShareBasic, $1.10) and net income ($736M) come from a different provenance family (Yahoo wire for net income vs SEC EDGAR for the per-share tags). Per ledger discipline this summary reports resolver/shard values as the KPI source of truth rather than silently substituting the release's number, but the $31M gap (plausibly preferred-stock dividends deducted between consolidated net income and net income available to common shareholders, though the release does not itself show that reconciliation step) is flagged here rather than smoothed over.
